items.title: The parabolic Hecke module and the antispherical standard basis
items.statement: Work with the normalized type-$A$ Hecke algebra $H_v(n)$ over $A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ of [[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]: generators $H_s$ with $H_s^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_s$, standard basis $\{H_w:w\in S_n\}$, bar involution $\overline{H_s}=H_s^{-1}=H_s-(v^{-1}-v)$ and Kazhdan-Lusztig basis $\{\underline H_w\}$ of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] (so that $\underline H_s=H_s+v$). Fix $J\subseteq S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$, let $W_J=\langle s:s\in J\rangle\subseteq S_n$ be the standard parabolic subgroup and let $\Phi_J$ be its root subsystem, all in the conventions of [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]. Two characters of the parabolic Hecke algebra $H_J\subseteq H_v(n)$ are used. For $s\in J$ the quadratic relation makes $v^{-1}$ and $-v$ the two roots of $x^2-(v^{-1}-v)x-1=0$, so there are well-defined algebra homomorphisms $\varphi_{+},\varphi_{-}:H_J\to A$ with $\varphi_+(H_s)=v^{-1}$ and $\varphi_-(H_s)=-v$ for all $s\in J$ (they respect the braid relations because they are scalar on the generators). Viewing $A$ through $\varphi_+$ (resp. $\varphi_-$) as a right $H_J$-module gives the **spherical parabolic module** $M^J:=A\otimes_{H_J}H_v(n)$ and the **antispherical parabolic module** $N^J:=A\otimes_{H_J}H_v(n)$, right $H_v(n)$-modules under right multiplication on the second factor. Throughout, $\Phi^+$ is the positive system of $\Phi$ and $\Phi_J^+=\Phi_J\cap\Phi^+$, and $$^JW:=\{w\in S_n:\ell(sw)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in J\},\qquad W^J:=\{w\in S_n:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in J\}$$ are the minimal left and right coset representatives; by [[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] and [[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]] every $w\in S_n$ factors uniquely as $w=l y$ with $l\in W_J$, $y\in{^JW}$ and $\ell(w)=\ell(l)+\ell(y)$, and inversion interchanges ${^JW}$ and $W^J$. The definitions of $\varphi_\pm$ use only the quadratic relation on generators; no further module-theoretic input enters.
items.strategy: Conventions and well-definedness only. The signs $v^{-1},-v$ solve $t^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)t$ by direct expansion ([[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]), so $\varphi_\pm$ are algebra maps because the Hecke relations in a single factor are generated by the quadratic relations together with the braid relations, on which scalars act trivially. The coset statements are the standard parabolic factorization of [[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]] and [[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]]; inversion preserves length and interchanges left and right descents, so ${^JW}^{-1}=W^J$. The bases $\{1\otimes H_x:x\in{^JW}\}$ and the right action formulas are asserted nowhere here: they are the content of [[lem-the-parabolic-hecke-modules-have-standard-bases-actions-and-compatible-bars]]. The spherical module is recorded because the singular-block multiplicities are read in the spherical normalization; the antispherical module is recorded because its canonical basis is the induced-sign analogue and its coefficients differ in general.

items.title: Standard bases, right actions and bar involutions on the parabolic Hecke modules
items.statement:
Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and put $m_x:=1\otimes H_x$, $n_x:=1\otimes H_x$ for $x\in{^JW}$, and $C_s:=\underline H_s=H_s+v$ for $s\in S$. (1) (Bases.) The sets $\{m_x:x\in{^JW}\}$ and $\{n_x:x\in{^JW}\}$ are $A$-bases of $M^J$ and $N^J$ respectively: indeed every $w\in S_n$ factors uniquely as $w=ly$ with $l\in W_J$, $y\in{^JW}$, length-additively, and $\varphi_\pm(H_l)=\varphi_\pm(H_s)^{\ell(l)}\in\{v^{-\ell(l)},\pm v^{\ell(l)}\}$ is a unit of $A$, so $1\otimes H_w=\varphi_\pm(H_l)\,(1\otimes H_y)$ in both modules. (2) (Right action.) For $s\in S$ and $x\in{^JW}$: $$m_x C_s= egin{cases}m_{xs}+v\,m_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs>x,\ m_{xs}+v^{-1}m_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs<x,\ (v+v^{-1})m_x,&xs
otin{^JW},\end{cases}\qquad n_xC_s= egin{cases}n_{xs}+v\,n_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs>x,\ n_{xs}+v^{-1}n_x,&xs\in{^JW},\ xs<x,\ 0,&xs
otin{^JW}.\end{cases}$$ (3) (Bar.) The assignment $a\otimes h\mapsto  ar a\otimes ar h$ (bar on $A$ and the bar involution of $H_v(n)$) descends to $A$-antilinear involutions of $M^J$ and $N^J$ that satisfy $\overline{X\cdot h}=\overline X\cdot ar h$ and $\overline{m_x}=m_x+\sum_{y<x}a_{y,x}m_y$, $\overline{n_x}=n_x+\sum_{y<x}b_{y,x}n_y$ with $a_{y,x},b_{y,x}\in A$ and $a_{x,x}=b_{x,x}=1$; the top coefficient is one. (4) (Parabolic property.) If $x\in{^JW}$ and $s\in S$ with $xs
otin{^JW}$ then $xs=rx$ for a unique $r\in W_J$ and $xs>x$.
items.strategy: Direct computation from the standard basis and the defining relations. (1) is the length-additive factorization of [[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]] and [[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] together with $1\otimes H_l=\varphi_\pm(H_l)(1\otimes1)$; injectivity of the resulting triangular transition is immediate from the units $\varphi_\pm(H_l)$. (2) The standard right multiplication rules $H_xH_s=H_{xs}$ for $xs>x$ and $H_xH_s=H_{xs}+(v^{-1}-v)H_x$ for $xs<x$ of [[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]] give the displayed formulas when $xs\in{^JW}$. In the remaining case $xs\notin{^JW}$ the parabolic property (4) gives $xs=rx$ with $r\in W_J$ and $\ell(xs)=\ell(x)+1$, so $n_xC_s=n_xH_s+vn_x$; the relation $H_{xs}=H_rH_x$ and $H_xH_s=H_{xs}+(v^{-1}-v)H_x$ give $n_xH_s=1\otimes H_{xs}+(v^{-1}-v)n_x=(-v+(v^{-1}-v))n_x=-v^{-1}n_x$, whence $n_xC_s=0$; in the spherical case the same computation returns $(v+v^{-1})m_x$ because $\varphi_+(H_r)=v^{-1}$. (3) The bar on $H_v(n)$ is a semilinear involution ([[lem-the-hecke-bar-involution-is-well-defined]]) and $\varphi_u(\bar h)=\overline{\varphi_u(h)}$ for $h\in H_J$ and $u\in\{+,-\}$ because $\overline H_s=H_s-(v^{-1}-v)$ maps to $\overline{-v}=-v^{-1}$ and to $\overline{v^{-1}}=v$; hence the assignment is balanced over $H_J$ and descends. The expansion of $\overline{m_x}=1\otimes\overline{H_x}$ has top term $1\otimes H_x$: $\overline{H_x}=H_{x^{-1}}^{-1}=H_{x^{-1}}+\sum_{z<x^{-1}}c_zH_z$ with $c_z\in v^{-1}\mathbb Z[v^{-1}]$ by the quadratic relations, the term with $z=x^{-1}$ is the only one whose coset factor can contribute $m_x$, and all other terms lie in the $A$-span of the $m_y$ with $y<x$ because the Bruhat order is inverted and the coset factorization is length-additive; the coefficient of $m_x$ is the unit $\varphi_u(H_l)$ with $l=1$. The parabolic property (4) is the standard fact that $x\in{^JW}$ and $xs\notin{^JW}$ force $xs=rx$ with $r\in W_J$ ([[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]]); this is the only place where the coset combinatorics of the parabolic enters.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig bases
items.statement: Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and [[lem-the-parabolic-hecke-modules-have-standard-bases-actions-and-compatible-bars]]. For every $x\in{^JW}$ there is a unique $C_x\in M^J$ and a unique $D_x\in N^J$ with (i) $\overline{C_x}=C_x$ and $\overline{D_x}=D_x$, and (ii) $C_x\in m_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]\,m_y$, $D_x\in n_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]\,n_y$, the sums over the lower Bruhat ideal of $x$ inside ${^JW}$. The sets $\{C_x\}_{x\in{^JW}}$ and $\{D_x\}_{x\in{^JW}}$ are $A$-bases of $M^J$ and $N^J$. No coefficientwise positivity is asserted.
items.strategy: The triangular induction of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] applies verbatim over the finite Bruhat ideal, because the only inputs are the bar involution and the fact that the bar of a standard basis element has top term itself with coefficient one and lies in the span of lower standard elements: for $\overline{m_x}=m_x+\sum_{y<x}a_{y,x}m_y$ as in [[lem-the-parabolic-hecke-modules-have-standard-bases-actions-and-compatible-bars]], one defines the coefficients of $C_x$ by descending induction on $\ell(x)$ through the finite interval $\{y\in{^JW}:y\le x\}$, using the bar-duality equation; anti-invariance splits each coefficient into its positive- and negative-degree parts (the two intersections $v\mathbb Z[v]\cap v^{-1}\mathbb Z[v^{-1}]=0$), and the same uniqueness argument on a Bruhat-maximal support element applies. The sphere of the argument is dimension-free and finite, and no choice principle is used. The proof of the existence statement in [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] is the template; only the coefficient recursion changes its indexing set from $S_n$ to ${^JW}$.

items.title: The parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig bases and polynomials
items.statement: Retain the notation of the preceding items and write the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig bases of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] as $$C_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{^JW}}m_{y,x}\,m_y,\qquad D_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{^JW}}n_{y,x}\,n_y,\qquad x\in{^JW},$$ with coefficients $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in\mathbb Z[v]$ supported on the lower Bruhat ideal, $m_{x,x}=n_{x,x}=1$ and $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<x$. The **spherical parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials** are $M^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}m_{y,x}$ with $q=v^{-2}$, and the **antispherical (sign) parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials** are $N^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}n_{y,x}$; the parity clause of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] makes these polynomials in $q$. Normalization dictionary (the exact Deodhar normalization): with $P^J_{y,x}(u)$ the parabolic polynomials of Deodhar (1987) attached to the subset $J$, one has $M^J_{y,x}=P^J_{y^{-1},x^{-1}}$ for $u=-1$ and $N^J_{y,x}=P^J_{y^{-1},x^{-1}}$ for $u=q$, in the index convention of Deodhar and of the anti-spherical category. Values at $v=1$ are written $m_{y,x}(1)$, $n_{y,x}(1)$. The spherical coefficients reduce to ordinary ones: if $W_J$ is finite with longest element $w_0^J$ then $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^J y,\,w_0^J x}$ for all $y,x\in{^JW}$, where $p$ is the coefficient of the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].
items.strategy: Definitions and normalization only. The coefficients are those of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], so their support, diagonal value and $v\mathbb Z[v]$ property are inherited, and the substitution $q=v^{-2}$ is integral because the coefficient has fixed parity. The Deodhar dictionary is a normalization statement: the comparison of the two induced modules with Deodhar's spherical and sign modules, in the parameter translation recorded in the anti-spherical category reference, is used only to fix exponents; the spherical-to-ordinary reduction $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^J y,w_0^J x}$ is quoted from the same source and is the specialization of the spherical module to ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig combinatorics, not a new computation. The naming is fixed as follows: spherical = induced from the character $H_s\mapsto v^{-1}$ (the trivial representation), antispherical or sign = induced from $H_s\mapsto -v$.

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials are alternating sums of ordinary ones
items.statement: Retain the notation of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]. (1) (Antispherical alternating sum.) For all $x,y\in{^JW}$, $$n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}\,v^{\ell(z)}\,p_{zy,\,x},$$ the sum over all $z\in W_J$ (the product $zy$ taken in $S_n$, and $p_{\cdot,x}$ the ordinary coefficient of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], so the inner coefficients vanish unless $zy\le x$). (2) (Spherical reduction.) If $W_J$ is finite with longest element $w_0^J$ then for all $x,y\in{^JW}$ $$m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^J y,\ w_0^J x}.$$ In particular both families are computable from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, with no separate recursion.
items.strategy: Both parts follow from the induced-module description and uniqueness. For (2): left multiplication by $w_0^J$ is a bijection $W_J\to W_J$ with $\ell(w_0^Jl)=\ell(w_0^J)-\ell(l)$, and the element $\sum_{l}\varphi_+(H_l)(1\otimes H_{l^{-1}y})$ identifies the spherical module with the span of the ordinary basis elements indexed by $w_0^J{^JW}$; comparing with the ordinary $\underline H$-basis ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]) and using the index symmetry $p_{a^{-1},b^{-1}}=p_{a,b}$ gives $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ (this is the standard reduction quoted in the anti-spherical reference). For (1): the $A$-linear map $\Phi:H_v(n)\to N^J$, $h\mapsto1\otimes h$, is bar-equivariant, and $\Phi(\underline H_x)=\sum_{w}p_{w,x}(1\otimes H_w)$; collecting by coset, $1\otimes H_{zy}=\varphi_-(H_z)(1\otimes H_y)=(-v)^{\ell(z)}n_y$ whenever $zy$ factors length-additively with $z\in W_J$, $y\in{^JW}$, so $\Phi(\underline H_x)=\sum_{y\in{^JW}}c_y n_y$ with $c_y=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{zy,x}$. This element is bar-invariant (image of a bar-invariant element under a bar-equivariant map, part (3) of the standard-basis lemma) and its coefficient at $n_x$ is $p_{x,x}=1$; the defining properties of $D_x$ in [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] (bar-invariance, top coefficient one, lower coefficients in $v\mathbb Z[v]$) then give $\Phi(\underline H_x)=D_x$ by uniqueness, and comparing coefficients with the expansion of $D_x$ yields $n_{y,x}=c_y$. The divisibility $c_y\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<x$ is the only point needing the coefficient bookkeeping of the ordinary recursion: it follows from the bar-invariance of $\Phi(\underline H_x)$ by splitting the coefficient of $n_y$ into its parts in $v\mathbb Z[v]$ and $v^{-1}\mathbb Z[v^{-1}]$ exactly as in the uniqueness argument of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. Both parts are finite computations inside the Hecke algebra.

items.title: The singular integral block and its dot stabilizer
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, simple roots $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n$, Weyl group $W$, Weyl vector $\rho$ and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$, as in [[def-bgg-category-o]] and [[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]. A weight $\mu$ is **dot-antidominant** if $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\le0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$ and **integral** if $\langle\mu,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ for all $i$ ([[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]], [[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]]). Fix such a weight $\mu$ and put $J=J(\mu):=\{i:\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=0\}$ and $W_\mu:=W_J=\langle s_i:i\in J\rangle$; then the dot stabilizer $\{v\in W:v\cdot\mu=\mu\}$ equals $W_J$ (the inclusion $W_J\subseteq$ stabilizer holds because each $s_i$, $i\in J$, fixes $\mu+\rho$; equality follows since the stabilizer of an integral antidominant weight is generated by the reflections it contains and is a standard parabolic, [[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]]). The **singular integral block** $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the block of [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]] of the central character of $\mu$; its simple objects $L(w\cdot\mu)$, standard objects $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)=M(w\cdot\mu)$, costandard objects $\nabla(w\cdot\mu)$ and projective covers $P(w\cdot\mu)$ are indexed by $w\in W$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], [[def-verma-module]]), and $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ if and only if $w'\in wW_J$. Hence the labels can be normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $w\in W^J=\{w:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \forall s\in J\}$, and inversion carries $W^J$ onto ${^JW}$ of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]]. The block is a highest-weight category with the standard and simple classes as bases of its Grothendieck group ([[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]), it satisfies BGG reciprocity $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]$, and the multiplicity matrix is unitriangular for the refinement of the dominance order on the dot orbit ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]). The block is **regular** when $J=\varnothing$ (no wall) and **singular** when $J\neq\varnothing$; all statements below are for the singular case, and the regular case is that of [[def-regular-integral-dot-orbit-labelling-convention]].
items.strategy: Conventions and inherited structure only. The stabilizer claim uses the standard fact that for an integral dot-antidominant weight the dot stabilizer is the standard parabolic generated by the simple reflections it contains ([[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]]); the coset description of the label set is $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu\iff w^{-1}w'\in W_\mu\iff w'\in wW_J$. The block theory, the index set $W$, the highest-weight structure, the Grothendieck bases and BGG reciprocity are quoted from the published items; no new multiplicity assertion is made here. The normalization by $W^J$ (rather than $W$) is recorded exactly because it matches the minimal coset representatives of the parabolic Hecke modules and the inversion dictionary $W^J={^JW}^{-1}$.

items.title: The facet tensor-weight exclusion lemma
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be an integral dot-antidominant dot-regular weight and let $\mu$ be an integral dot-antidominant weight such that the facet $F_\mu$ lies in the closure of the chamber $F_\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$ for the positive roots $\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ of the parabolic subsystem $\Phi_J$ of $J=J(\mu)$ defined in [[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]], and $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ has the same sign as $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ for every remaining positive root. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant weight of the linear orbit $W(\mu-\lambda)$ ([[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]]) and let $E=L(\nu)$ ([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]). Then for all $w,w'\in W$ and every weight $\gamma$ of $E$: if $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\lambda+\gamma$, then $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ and $\gamma=w(\mu-\lambda)$. Consequently, for every $w$ the tensor $E\otimes\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has exactly one Verma factor whose central character is that of $\mu$, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, and its multiplicity in the Verma flag computed by [[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]] is one.
items.strategy: The proof is the published single-wall proof of [[lem-single-wall-tensor-weight-exclusion]] with the stabilizer $\{1,s\}$ replaced by the full dot stabilizer $W_J$; only the last step changes. Write $\lambda_\bullet=\lambda+\rho$, $\mu_\bullet=\mu+\rho$. From $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\lambda+\gamma$ one gets $(w')^{-1}\gamma=\mu_\bullet-x\lambda_\bullet$ with $x=(w')^{-1}w$; the norm bound $|\gamma|\le|\nu|=|\mu_\bullet-\lambda_\bullet|$ ([[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]) and the dominant distance comparison for the dominant vectors $-\mu_\bullet,-\lambda_\bullet$ ([[lem-dominant-norm-distance-comparison]]) give equality throughout; the equality case gives $x(-\lambda_\bullet)\in \operatorname{Stab}_W(-\mu_\bullet)(-\lambda_\bullet)=W_J\,(-\lambda_\bullet)$, so $x\lambda_\bullet\in W_J\lambda_\bullet$, and since $\lambda_\bullet$ is regular, $x\in W_J$. Hence $x\cdot\mu=\mu$ (because $W_J$ is the dot stabilizer) and $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$, and $\gamma=w(\mu-\lambda)$; the multiplicity-one clause is [[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]. The central-character clause uses [[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]. The Choice assumption is inherited from the published translation and norm items; no new choice principle is used.

items.title: Translation to the wall on Verma, simple and projective objects
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]: $\lambda$ integral dot-antidominant and dot-regular, $\mu$ integral dot-antidominant with $F_\mu$ in the closure of the chamber $F_\lambda$, $J=J(\mu)$, $W_\mu=W_J$. Let $
u$ be the unique dominant weight of $W(\mu-\lambda)$ and let $$T:=T_\lambda^\mu=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(L(
u)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\mu,\qquad T':=T_\mu^\lambda,$$ be the translation functors of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], which are exact and biadjoint ([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]). Then: (1) $T\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and $T
abla(w\cdot\lambda)\cong
abla(w\cdot\mu)$ for every $w\in W$. (2) $TL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu)$ if $w\in W^J$, and $TL(w\cdot\lambda)=0$ otherwise; equivalently $TL(w\cdot\lambda)
eq0$ if and only if the facet $F_{w\cdot\mu}$ is contained in the upper closure $F^+_{w\cdot\lambda}$ of [[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]. (3) (Big projective on the wall.) Let $\Xi_\mu:=T_{-ho}^{\mu}L(-ho)$ be the translate of the simple object of the most singular block. Then $\Xi_\mu$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O_\mu$, it is the projective cover $P(1\cdot\mu)$ of $L(\mu)$, and $(\Xi_\mu:\Delta(w\cdot\mu))=1$ for every $w\in W$; consequently $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))\ge1$ for all $y,w\in W^J$ and $[\Delta(w\cdot\mu):L(\mu)]=1$ for all $w\in W$.
items.strategy:
Direct adaptation of the published single-wall proof, with the facet case. (1) By [[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]] the tensor $L(
u)\otimes\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities $\dim L(
u)_{\eta-w\cdot\lambda}$, and by [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]] exactly one of its factors has central character $\chi_\mu$, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, with multiplicity one; applying the exact projection $\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}$ keeps that factor and kills the others (the central-character projections are exact and a Verma flag restricts to a Verma flag of the projection, as in the published single-wall argument), giving $T\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ because a one-factor flag identifies the object. The dual statement follows from exactness of $T$ for the restricted duality and $TL(
u)^*$ adjunction, or by repeating the argument with $
abla$; both are recorded in the published single-wall theorem. (2) Exactness of $T$ and the surjection $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)	woheadrightarrow L(w\cdot\lambda)$ give a surjection $T\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)	woheadrightarrow TL(w\cdot\lambda)$ into $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, so $TL(w\cdot\lambda)$ is either $0$ or $L(w\cdot\mu)$, because $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ has simple head $L(w\cdot\mu)$ and its only simple quotient is $L(w\cdot\mu)$; the dichotomy is decided by the facet criterion. For the criterion: by [[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]] and [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]] the condition $F_{w\cdot\mu}\subseteq F^+_{w\cdot\lambda}$ is equivalent, on the sign pattern of $w(\mu+ho)$ and $w(\lambda+ho)$, to $w(\Phi_J^+)\subseteq\Phi^+$, i.e. to $\ell(ws)>\ell(w)$ for every $s\in J$, i.e. to $w\in W^J$; this is the standard descent characterization of minimal coset representatives. When $w
otin W^J$ there is $s\in J$ with $ws<w$; then $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)\hookrightarrow\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ is a proper embedding (Verma embedding criterion, strong linkage) which is sent to an isomorphism by $T$ because $T\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)=\Delta(ws\cdot\mu)=\Delta(w\cdot\mu)=T\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ (as $s$ fixes $\mu$), so $TL(w\cdot\lambda)=0$ since $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ is a quotient of $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)/\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$; this is the published argument for the single wall. (3) $L(-ho)$ is the unique simple of the semisimple most singular block and is both projective and injective there; $T_{-ho}^\mu$ is exact and preserves projectives and injectives by [[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]], so $\Xi_\mu$ is projective and injective. The Verma flag multiplicities $(\Xi_\mu:\Delta(w\cdot\mu))=1$ are the content of the published exercise: its hint reduces to the tensor flag computation of [[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]] with the translating weight of $(\pmho,\mu)$ for the single adjoint orbit of $ho$, and then to the comparison with the projective cover $P(1\cdot\mu)$ via BGG reciprocity ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]) and [[cor-antidominant-verma-modules-are-simple]]; the surjection $\Xi_\mu	woheadrightarrow\Delta(\mu)	woheadrightarrow L(\mu)$ and the multiplicity one show indecomposability. The remaining displayed consequences follow by BGG reciprocity and unipotence of the multiplicity one.

items.title: Singular category O multiplicities are parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig values
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]] with $J=J(\mu)$, so $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the singular integral block of [[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]] with labels normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $W^J$, and let $w_0$ be the longest element of $W$. Then for all $y,w\in W^J$ $$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=P_{y w_0,\ w w_0}(1),$$ the value at $q=1$ of the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial attached to the pair $(yw_0,ww_0)$ in the classical normalization of [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]. Equivalently, under the inversion dictionary $x\mapsto x^{-1}$ from $W^J$ to ${^JW}$ of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]], $$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=m_{w^{-1},\,y^{-1}}(1),$$ the value at $v=1$ of the **spherical** parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficient of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]; the **antispherical** coefficients $n_{u,v}$ give the multiplicity matrix of the mirror normalization (dominant-side block and the opposite parabolic) and differ from the spherical ones already for $S_3$ with $J=\{s_1\}$. In particular all singular multiplicities are computable from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, and no individual polynomial coefficients beyond the value at one occur.
items.strategy: Exactness plus the regular multiplicity theorem. Let $T=T_\lambda^\mu$. By [[thm-translation-to-the-wall-on-verma-simple-and-projective-objects]] one has $T M(y\cdot\lambda)=\Delta(y\cdot\mu)=M(y\cdot\mu)$ for every $y\in W$; since $T$ is exact, applying $T$ to a composition series of $M(y\cdot\lambda)$ yields a composition series of $M(y\cdot\mu)$ in which a simple $L(x\cdot\lambda)$ contributes $L(x\cdot\mu)$ if $x\in W^J$ and zero otherwise (again [[thm-translation-to-the-wall-on-verma-simple-and-projective-objects]]). Therefore $$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=\sum_{x\in W^J,\ x\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu}[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]$$ for $y,w\in W^J$; the constraint $x\in W^J$ and $x\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ forces $x=w$, because $x\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ means $x\in wW_J$ and $W^J\cap wW_J=\{w\}$. Hence $[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$, and the regular block's theorem [[thm-simple-verma-composition-multiplicities-are-kazhdan-lusztig-values]] applied in the antidominant realization gives $[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1)$: the antidominant relabelling of the regular block sends the dominant label $a$ to $aw_0$ (since $w\cdot(w_0\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}})=ww_0\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}}$), so the classical pair is $(yw_0,ww_0)$. The BGG-reciprocity form is [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]. The spherical normalization clause is the reduction $m_{u,v}=p_{w_0^Ju,w_0^Jv}$ of [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]] combined with the index dictionary $x\mapsto x^{-1}$; the stated disagreement with the antispherical family is the counterexample item. This proof uses only exactness, the standard theorem and the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig theorem; no localization, Koszul or Soergel-bimodule input enters.

items.title: Standard parabolic and Levi subalgebras from a subset of simple roots
items.statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, root system $\Phi$ in the abstract sense of [[def-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system]] identified with the root set of $\mathfrak g$ by [[thm-the-root-set-is-a-reduced-crystallographic-root-system]], positive system $\Phi^+$, simple roots $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\}$ and root spaces $\mathfrak g_\alpha$. Fix $J\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ and let $\Phi_J=\mathbb Z J\cap\Phi$ be the root subsystem generated by the simple roots in $J$, with $\Phi_J^\pm=\Phi_J\cap\Phi^\pm$ and Weyl group $W_J\subseteq W$ ([[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]). Define $$\mathfrak l_J:=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J}\mathfrak g_\alpha,\qquad \mathfrak u_J:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^+\setminus\Phi_J^+}\mathfrak g_\alpha,\qquad \mathfrak p_J:=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J.$$ Then: (1) $\mathfrak l_J$ is a reductive Lie subalgebra of $\mathfrak g$ with root system $\Phi_J$ and Cartan $\mathfrak h$; (2) $\mathfrak u_J$ is a Lie subalgebra, $[\mathfrak l_J,\mathfrak u_J]\subseteq\mathfrak u_J$, so $\mathfrak p_J\subseteq\mathfrak g$ is a Lie subalgebra; (3) $\mathfrak u_J$ is the nilradical of $\mathfrak p_J$ and $\mathfrak l_J$ is a Levi factor, so $\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ is a Levi decomposition ([[def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition]], [[def-nilradical-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]]); (4) $\mathfrak p_J$ contains the Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ of [[def-positive-and-negative-nilpotent-subalgebras-and-borel-subalgebra]] and $\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak b\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_J^-}\mathfrak g_\alpha$; (5) $\mathfrak p_\varnothing=\mathfrak b$ and $\mathfrak p_{\Delta}=\mathfrak g$, and $\mathfrak p_J$ depends only on the pair $(\Phi^+,J)$.
items.strategy: Standard root-space bookkeeping. (1)-(2) use the bracket rule $[\mathfrak g_\alpha,\mathfrak g_\beta]\subseteq\mathfrak g_{\alpha+\beta}$ and the fact that $\Phi_J$ is a root subsystem closed under addition when the sum is a root: for $\alpha,\beta\in\Phi_J$ with $\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$, the root $\alpha+\beta$ is an integral combination of $J$ and hence lies in $\Phi_J$; the Jacobi identity is inherited. (3) $\mathfrak u_J$ is an ideal because $[\mathfrak l_J,\mathfrak u_J]\subseteq\mathfrak u_J$ and $[\mathfrak u_J,\mathfrak u_J]\subseteq\mathfrak u_J$ (the sum of two positive roots outside $\Phi_J^+$ either is not a root or again lies outside), and it is nilpotent and maximal among nilpotent ideals since $\mathfrak p_J/\mathfrak u_J\cong\mathfrak l_J$ is reductive with no noncentral abelian ideal; the Levi decomposition is [[def-levi-subalgebra-and-levi-decomposition]]. (4)-(5) are immediate from the definitions and the standard identification of $\mathfrak b$. Existence of the root system data and the coroot pairings is [[thm-the-root-set-is-a-reduced-crystallographic-root-system]] and [[thm-simple-roots-form-a-basis-and-every-root-has-one-sign-of-integral-coordinates]]. This item is deliberately type-free and asserts no parabolic quotient geometry.

items.title: Parabolic category O for a standard parabolic
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published category-O theory. Let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ be the standard parabolic of [[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]], with Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and nilradical $\mathfrak u_J$, and $W_J$ its Weyl group. A weight $\lambda$ is **$\mathfrak p$-dominant** if $\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for all $\alpha\in\Phi_J^+$ (this is dominance for the Levi root system; in particular $\lambda$ is integral for $\Phi_J$). For such a $\lambda$ let $E(\lambda)$ be the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak p$-module obtained from the finite-dimensional simple $\mathfrak l_J$-module of highest weight $\lambda$ ([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]) by letting $\mathfrak u_J$ act by zero, and define the **generalized Verma module** $$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}E(\lambda).$$ The **parabolic category** $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is the full subcategory of $\mathcal O$ whose objects are the finitely generated $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-modules on which $U(\mathfrak p)$ acts locally finitely; its objects are exactly the modules $M\in\mathcal O$ such that every vector lies in a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule. For each $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the module $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, has highest weight $\lambda$, and $M(\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of the Verma module $M(\lambda)$ that lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. The simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are the simple highest-weight modules $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$ $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral, and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions in $\mathcal O$. The costandard objects are the dual module quotients $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ obtained by restricted duality from $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$.
items.strategy: Definitional setup, with the two structural assertions deferred. The finiteness and local-finiteness conditions are read off from [[def-bgg-category-o]]; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is a quotient of $M(\lambda)$ because the $\mathfrak p$-submodule $E(\lambda)$ has the one-dimensional highest weight space as a $\mathfrak p$-quotient, and induction is right exact. That $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest such quotient, and that the simple objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ are exactly the $L(\lambda)$ with $\lambda$ $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral, are proved in [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]] and asserted here only as notation. The closure under subobjects, quotients and extensions is immediate from local finiteness of a direct summand of a sum. No highest-weight or projective statement is made here.

items.title: Parabolic category O is a highest weight category
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then: (1) (Simples.) Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form. (2) (Standards.) For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and $[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]
eq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of $M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. (3) (Enough projectives.) The inclusion $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint $L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient); $L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$ to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object $P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives. (4) (BGG reciprocity and duality.) For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda,\mu$, $$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$ the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $
abla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),
abla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$ for all $\lambda,\mu$.
items.strategy: Subcategory and reflector arguments. (1) A highest-weight vector of $L(\lambda)$ generates a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak u_J$-module only if $\mathfrak u_J$ acts by zero on it, and it generates a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak l_J$-module exactly when $\lambda$ is $\Phi_J$-dominant integral; conversely for such $\lambda$ the finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-integrability of $L(\lambda)$ follows from the fact that $L(\lambda)$ is a quotient of the induced module from a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module (the case $\mathfrak g$ simple or the use of the Morita/duality argument). The remaining simples lie outside because a nonzero $\mathfrak u_J$-nilpotent vector of weight $\lambda$ in $L(\lambda)$ would give a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-submodule whose Levi weights contradict $\Phi_J$-dominance. (2) $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the quotient of $M(\lambda)$ by the submodule generated over $U(\mathfrak g)$ by the vectors of the maximal $\mathfrak p$-proper part; the head and dominance claims are the standard highest weight facts and the finiteness of length is inherited from [[thm-every-category-o-object-has-finite-length]]. (3) The functor $L_{\mathfrak p}$ exists because $\mathcal O$ has finite length and the sum of all submodules with $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient has a universal maximal object (the standard Serre-subcategory reflector; every object of $\mathcal O$ has finite length by [[thm-every-category-o-object-has-finite-length]]). Exactness of the inclusion is clear, so $L_{\mathfrak p}$ as a left adjoint is right exact and carries projective objects to projective objects; the module $L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ then maps onto $L_{\mathfrak p}(L(\lambda))=L(\lambda)$, and its indecomposability and essentiality follow from the corresponding properties of the $\mathcal O$-projective cover ([[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]]) applied to a length-minimal lift. (4) The reciprocity is the standard highest-weight-category argument: $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)]$ by [[lem-hom-from-projectives-counts-simple-composition-factors]], while $(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))$ for a standard-filtered projective, using the standard/costandard Ext-vanishing of [[lem-standard-costandard-hom-and-ext-vanishing]] restricted to the Serre subcategory; the identification of the two Hom spaces through the inclusion $M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu)\hookrightarrow\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu)$ is the usual BGG argument. Restricted duality preserves local finiteness and exchanges standards and costandards ([[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]]). All sums are finite because composition multiplicities in $\mathcal O$ are finite.

items.title: Parabolic category O multiplicities are parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig values
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_J$ be a standard parabolic in type $A_{n-1}$ with Levi Weyl group $W_J$, longest element $w_0^J$ and the sets ${^JW}\subseteq W$ of minimal left coset representatives and $W^J={^JW}^{-1}$, and let $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ be the parabolic category of [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] in a fixed integral block. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda,\mu$ let $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ be the generalized Verma and the projective cover of [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]. Then for $y,x\in{^JW}$ the multiplicities are the values at $v=1$ of the **spherical** parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]: $$[M_{\mathfrak p}(w_0^J y):L(w_0^J x)]=(P^{\mathfrak p}(w_0^J x):M_{\mathfrak p}(w_0^J y))=m_{x,y}(1),$$ the index shift $\xi\mapsto w_0^J\xi$ being the exact longest-coset shift between the minimal representatives ${^JW}$ of the Hecke module and the standard modules of the parabolic category. Equivalently $[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]=m_{\mu^\sharp,\lambda^\sharp}(1)$ where $\lambda^\sharp,\mu^\sharp\in{^JW}$ are the minimal coset representatives $\lambda^\sharp=w_0^J\lambda$ (and the multiplicity vanishes unless $\mu\le\lambda$, compatibly with the unitriangular order). In particular the parabolic multiplicities are computable from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$ by the spherical reduction, and by BGG reciprocity the projective-standard multiplicities coincide with them.
items.strategy: The statement is the type-A form of the categorification of the parabolic Hecke module. Route: (i) the spherical parabolic Hecke module $M^J$ of [[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] has standard basis indexed by ${^JW}$ and canonical basis the KL-Deodhar basis of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]; (ii) the Grothendieck-group comparison of the parabolic category sends the standard module $M_{\mathfrak p}(w_0^Jx)$ to the shifted standard basis vector and the projective module $P^{\mathfrak p}(w_0^Jx)$ to the canonical basis vector, so the transition matrix is the spherical coefficient matrix with the longest-coset shift; (iii) the values at one agree with the singular-block values of [[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]]. Step (ii) is the exact content to be proved locally: it says that wall-crossing translation functors act on the Grothendieck group of the parabolic category by multiplication by $C_s=\underline H_s$ with standards matching the standard basis and indecomposable projectives matching the self-dual basis. The source treatment proves this for the properly stratified parabolic subcategory of the principal block together with its equivalence to the singular central character; that equivalence is not scaffolded on this page. The item is therefore recorded escalated: the missing local prerequisite is a wall-crossing identification of the parabolic standard/simple multiplicity matrix with the singular block matrix, to be placed on this same A page before this item. Everything else (the polynomial families, the longest-coset shift, the BGG form) is fixed by the listed dependencies.

items.title: The parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig character formula
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, and retain the notation of [[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]], so that in the fixed integral block the matrix $S:=(m_{y,x}(1))$ indexed by ${^JW}\times{^JW}$ is unitriangular for the Bruhat order and $[M_{\mathfrak p}(w_0^J y):L(w_0^J x)]=S_{x,y}$. Then for every $x\in{^JW}$ the class of the simple module in the Grothendieck group of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, equivalently its formal character, is $$\mathrm{ch}\,L(w_0^J x)=\sum_{y\in{^JW}}S^{-1}_{y,x}\,\mathrm{ch}\,M_{\mathfrak p}(w_0^J y),$$ where $S^{-1}_{y,x}\in\mathbb Z$ are the entries of the inverse unitriangular matrix, computed by the finite chain recursion of [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] and [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-inversion-formula]] applied to the spherical parabolic coefficients; the sum is supported on $y\le x$. In particular the simple characters of the parabolic category are finitely determined by the parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig matrix, and no grading on $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is constructed.
items.strategy: Linear algebra over the unitriangular matrix. By [[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] the transition matrix from standard to simple characters is the transpose $(m_{x,y}(1))_{y,x}$ of the spherical coefficient matrix evaluated at one, unitriangular with diagonal one and support $x\le y$ ([[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]); the Grothendieck group of the block has the simple and standard classes as bases and the character map is linear ([[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]], [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]], [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]). Inverting the finite unitriangular system by the chain recursion of [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] and [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-inversion-formula]] gives the formula; the support clause is unitriangularity. The inversion itself is elementary and choice-free; the item inherits the escalation status of [[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] because its displayed matrix is that item's conclusion. No positivity of the inverse coefficients and no Ext or Koszul grading is asserted.

items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials for S_3 modulo S_2
items.statement: Take $W=S_3$ with simple reflections $s_1,s_2$, let $J=\{s_1\}$, so $W_J=\{1,s_1\}$ and the minimal left coset representatives are ${^JW}=\{e,\ s_2,\ s_2s_1\}$. In the notation of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] the two parabolic families are computed from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_3$ (all ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of comparable pairs in $S_3$ equal $1$): the **antispherical (sign)** coefficients are $$n_{e,e}=1,\quad n_{e,s_2}=v,\quad n_{e,s_2s_1}=0,\quad n_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$ all other coefficients being zero; the **spherical** coefficients are $$m_{e,e}=1,\quad m_{e,s_2}=v,\quad m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2},\quad m_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$ all other coefficients being zero. At $v=1$ the antispherical matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and the spherical matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ in the order $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$. The two families therefore already differ for this smallest nontrivial parabolic: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=0$ while $m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$.
items.strategy: Finite computation inside $H_v(3)$. The ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_3$ are known from [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] and the fact that all ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials of $S_3$ equal $1$: $p_{y,x}=v^{\ell(x)-\ell(y)}$ for $y\le x$ and zero otherwise, so the only nonzero values needed are $p_{e,e}=1$, $p_{e,s_1}=p_{e,s_2}=v$, $p_{e,s_1s_2}=p_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$, $p_{e,w_0}=v^{3}$, $p_{s_1,s_1s_2}=p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v$, $p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$, $p_{s_2,s_1s_2}=p_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v$, $p_{s_2,w_0}=v^{2}$, $p_{s_1s_2,w_0}=p_{s_2s_1,w_0}=v$, and the diagonal ones $1$. The antispherical coefficients are the alternating sums $n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{zy,x}$ of [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]. For $y=e$: $n_{e,e}=p_{e,e}=1$, $n_{e,s_2}=p_{e,s_2}=v$, and $n_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v\cdot v=0$. For $y=s_2$: $n_{s_2,s_2}=p_{s_2,s_2}-v\,p_{s_1s_2,s_2}=1$ (the second term vanishes since $\ell(s_1s_2)>\ell(s_2)$), and $n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=p_{s_2,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1s_2,s_2s_1}=v-0=v$, the second term vanishing because $s_1s_2$ and $s_2s_1$ are distinct of equal length. For $y=s_2s_1$: $n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=p_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{w_0,s_2s_1}=1-0=1$, the second term vanishing by the support condition. The spherical coefficients are $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ with $w_0^J=s_1$ ([[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]): $m_{e,e}=p_{s_1,s_1}=1$, $m_{e,s_2}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2}=v$, $m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$, $m_{s_2,s_2}=p_{s_1s_2,s_1s_2}=1$, $m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1s_2,w_0}=v$, $m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=p_{w_0,w_0}=1$. All arithmetic is in $\mathbb Z[v]$ with the Bruhat comparabilities of $S_3$ ([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]]); the coset set is ${^JW}=\{e,s_2,s_2s_1\}$ ([[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]). An independent construction of the two canonical bases in the normalized Hecke algebra of $S_3$, from the bar involution and the induced-module standard bases, reproduces both tables.

items.title: Translation to a singular wall in type A_2
items.statement: Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and use the coordinate $l=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$, so the dot action is $s\cdot l=-l-2$ and the facets are $(-\infty,-1)$, $\{-1\}$, $(-1,\infty)$ ([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]], Example 3.11 of the source). Take $\lambda=-2$, $\mu=-1$. Then the singular block $\mathcal O_{-1}$ has the single simple $L(-1)=M(-1)=P(-1)$, and the translation functor $T=T_{-2}^{-1}$ satisfies $T\,M(-2)=M(-1)$, $T\,M(0)=M(-1)$, $$T\,L(-2)=L(-1)\quad(\text{the label }1\in W^J),\qquad T\,L(0)=0\quad(\text{the label }s\notin W^J),$$ and $T\,P(-2)=2\,P(-1)$, because the projective cover $P(-2)$ of $L(-2)$ has the Verma flag $\Delta(-2),\Delta(0)$ and both factors are sent to $\Delta(-1)$. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$ take $J=\{s_1\}$ and the dot-antidominant $\mu$ with $\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$; then $W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$ and by [[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] the composition and Verma-flag matrices of the singular block are $$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$$ in the row/column order $(1,\,s_2,\,s_1s_2)$: explicitly $M(\mu)$ is irreducible, $M(s_2\cdot\mu)$ has composition factors $L(\mu),L(s_2\cdot\mu)$ once each, and $M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has all three simples once; dually $(P(\mu):\Delta(\mu))=1$, $(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(\mu))=(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_2\cdot\mu))=1$, $(P(s_1s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for all $y\in W^J$. The surviving simple labels are exactly the minimal coset representatives, so translation onto the wall kills $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\notin W^J$ (for instance $L(s_1\cdot\lambda)$ and $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ case).
items.strategy: Direct enumeration with the wall-translation theorem. The $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ part: $L(-2)=M(-2)$ and $L(0)$ are the two simples of the principal block and $M(0)$ has composition factors $L(0),L(-2)$ once each ([[cor-antidominant-verma-modules-are-simple]] and the standard $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ block structure); the survival criterion $w\in W^J$ of [[thm-translation-to-the-wall-on-verma-simple-and-projective-objects]] gives $TL(-2)=L(-1)$ and $TL(0)=0$, which also matches Example 3.16 of the source; the projective statement follows from the Verma flag of $P(-2)$ ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]) and the Verma clause of the wall-translation theorem. The $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ part: the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig data of the regular block enter through $P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1)$, and in $S_3$ these are all $1$ for comparable pairs, so the matrix is the transpose of the Bruhat-incidence matrix of $W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$; the computation was checked independently in the Hecke algebra of $S_3$. The dominance order on the weights $1\cdot\mu=-(4\alpha_1+5\alpha_2)/3$, $s_2\cdot\mu=(-4\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)/3$, $s_1s_2\cdot\mu=(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)/3$ confirms the support: $s_2\cdot\mu-\mu=\alpha_2$, $s_1s_2\cdot\mu-\mu=\alpha_1+\alpha_2$, $s_1s_2\cdot\mu-s_2\cdot\mu=\alpha_1$, all in $Q^+$, and no other pairs are linked.

items.title: A small parabolic category O character formula
items.statement: In the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ singular block at $\mu$ with $\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$ of [[ex-translation-to-a-singular-wall-in-type-a-two]], the multiplicity matrix $A:=(P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1))_{y,w\in W^J}$ in the order $(1,s_2,s_1s_2)$ is $$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-1&1&0\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}.$$ Hence in the Grothendieck group of the singular block $$\mathrm{ch}\,L(\mu)=\mathrm{ch}\,M(\mu),\qquad \mathrm{ch}\,L(s_2\cdot\mu)=\mathrm{ch}\,M(s_2\cdot\mu)-\mathrm{ch}\,M(\mu),\qquad \mathrm{ch}\,L(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\mathrm{ch}\,M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)-\mathrm{ch}\,M(s_2\cdot\mu).$$ The inverse coefficients are the Möbius values of the chain $1<s_2<s_1s_2$: the transition matrix is unitriangular, and each simple character is a finite signed combination of Verma characters supported on the Bruhat interval above the label. This is the smallest instance of the parabolic character formula of [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-character-formula]]; no coefficient outside $\{0,\pm1\}$ occurs in this block.
items.strategy: Explicit inversion of the $3\times3$ unitriangular matrix, using that all ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of $S_3$ are $1$ so that $A$ is the Bruhat-incidence matrix of the chain $W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$ ([[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]], [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]). The character identity is the matrix identity read in the Grothendieck group with its simple and standard bases ([[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]], [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]); the inverse is computed by the finite chain recursion of [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] and [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-inversion-formula]], which here reduces to $A^{-1}_{x,y}=-\sum_{x<z\le y}A^{-1}_{x,z}A_{z,y}$ with diagonal one. The Bruhat relations inside $W^J$ used are $1<s_2<s_1s_2$ and $1<s_1s_2$ ([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]); the weights of the three compositions were listed in [[ex-translation-to-a-singular-wall-in-type-a-two]].

items.title: Spherical and antispherical normalizations give different polynomials
items.statement: For $W=S_3$ and $J=\{s_1\}$ the spherical and antispherical parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] are not the same, and not merely by a unit: for the pair $y=e$, $x=s_2s_1\in{^JW}$ one has $$n_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v^{2}=0\neq m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2},$$ evaluated at $v=1$: the antispherical value vanishes while the spherical value is $1$. The value $n_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=0$ is not a unit multiple of $m_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=1$, and the two coefficients differ as polynomials, so the discrepancy is not an artifact of specializing at $v=1$. Consequently the two normalizations cannot be substituted for one another in a multiplicity statement: a singular-block or parabolic multiplicity theorem must fix the side of the parabolic and the corresponding module (trivial versus sign). In particular the singular-block multiplicity theorem of this page is stated in the spherical normalization and its mirror (dominant-side, opposite parabolic) form in the antispherical one, so using the antispherical value $n_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=0$ in place of the spherical $m_{e,s_2s_1}(1)=1$ produces a false multiplicity.
items.strategy: Two-term computation in the Hecke algebra of $S_3$, using the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients $p_{r,s}=v^{\ell(s)-\ell(r)}$ for comparable pairs and zero otherwise. Antispherical: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=\sum_{z\in\{1,s_1\}}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{z,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}$ by [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]; here $p_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$ and $s_1\le s_2s_1$ with length gap one, so $p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v$ and $n_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v^{2}=0$. Spherical: $m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$ by the reduction $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ with $w_0^J=s_1$. The coset set and Bruhat relations are those of [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]] and [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]; the values were checked by an independent construction of the two canonical bases in the normalized Hecke algebra of $S_3$ via the triangular construction of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. The conclusion is a counterexample to any normalization-blind statement of the parabolic multiplicity theorem, not to the theorems themselves.
